analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: USTs opened with a modest bid after Wednesday's bull-flattening move, helped by softer Australian employment data. DXY trades around 103.80 after testing 104.

Mizuho sees equities and oil as the key drivers of duration today. S&P and Nasdaq futures are back in the green after the overnight digestion of Anthropic's IPO. A risk-on tone into New York should cap how far the duration rally can extend.
Brent holds around $92.5 despite reports that Trump is considering a new round of strikes on Iran. A move back toward $100 would quickly revive the bearish-duration trade.

The FOMC minutes were clearly hawkish. Almost all participants expect further tightening and a couple see scope for 50bp in December. This was consistent with recent Fed speak and did little to shift December pricing.

The strategist sees 5% as the key level in 10Y UST yields. They are reluctant to chase a duration rally below it, particularly if equities and oil hold, and prefer selling strength ahead of next week's 2s/5s/7s supply.

Bund 10Y yields are around 3.37% after another wide 3.35-3.40% Wednesday range. French and Spanish auctions are likely to keep some pressure on euro-area government bonds. EUR/USD trades around 1.0975.

The ECB is reportedly discussing raising the minimum reserve requirement from 1% to 2%. Another 1% would lock up roughly €175bn against just over €2tn of excess liquidity, so a meaningful funding squeeze is unlikely. Mizuho sees the effect mainly in market plumbing: a positive EURUSD cross-currency basis at the very front end and some widening risk in the €STR-Euribor basis, small while excess liquidity is abundant. The effect becomes increasingly non-linear as liquidity falls.

On the BoE, upside inflation risks are building and wage growth is sticky, but there is no clear evidence of second-round effects. Mizuho thinks the BoE can afford to wait, as the labour market is looser than in the 2022-23 shock.
10Y Gilt yields rejected 5.30% resistance on Wednesday after softer services CPI, with 5.20% the next level to watch. GBP/USD trades around 1.3150 after testing 1.3125.
Asian equities were mixed as early Anthropic optimism faded. JGBs bull-flattened in a catch-up move to USTs, helped by stronger 25Y+ Rinban results. USD/JPY rose toward 159.75.
